subject: general
question: The cost price of a toy car is 80% of its selling price. If the selling price is ₹100, what is the profit percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

CP = 80% of SP ⇒ CP = 80

SP = 100

Profit = 100 − 80 = 20

Profit% = (20 ÷ 80) × 100 = 25%

**∴ Answer = 25%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

SP = 100, CP = 80% of SP

**Formula used:**

Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ CP = 80% of 100 = 80

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 100 − 80 = 20

⇒ Profit% = (20 ÷ 80) × 100

⇒ = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit Formula

Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

Relation

CP = given percentage of SP

Quick Trick

Assume SP = 100 for easy calculation

Concept

Profit is always calculated on CP
